error_signature: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/batched.py:127, if rows == 0
blocker_detail: The prototype reaches BATCHED_MARLIN and BatchedPrepareAndFinalize on TP=2 no-DP EP, but vLLM's reference BatchedPrepareAndFinalize.prepare builds the expert queue with a Python loop over experts, torch.count_nonzero, dynamic masked indexing, and a Python branch on the GPU scalar rows. During FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graph capture, that scalar branch is illegal, so the engine fails before API readiness and c512 cannot be measured on the production-equivalent graph path.
required_next_code_change: Replace the reference Python BatchedPrepareAndFinalize.prepare path with a graph-capturable no-DP expert queue builder and scatter/gather adapter for MXFP4 BatchedMarlin: compute per-local-expert token counts, compact token rows into [local_experts,max_tokens,K], and finalize back to [tokens,K] without host scalar reads.
interpretation: This proves the missing vLLM performance primitive is not just a backend selection flag. The backend can be selected, but the available reference batched prepare/finalize implementation is not CUDA-graph compatible and cannot serve as the c512 production lane. The promising next experiment is a graph-safe no-DP expert queue/scatter adapter, then rerun c512 against 174.190 tok/s.
